one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings fall inside the window (sources disagree: Oct 29 after close or Nov 3 pre-market; both before Nov 4) [9]. Guide was GB $58.25-60.25B, adj. EBITDA $2.86-2.96B, non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88 [1]; Uber has beaten its own guide consistently, but the stock has often fallen on prints (Q2 2026 guide read as light, AV capex narrative). The Q4 guide and any update on AV spend/Delivery Hero financing will dominate. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends Nov 5 [2], one day after the window, so little incremental. Alt data is mildly positive (Sept app downloads ~281k/day, +43% m/m per AltIndex [15]) but single-source and noisy. Robotaxi headline flow (Tesla Cybercab, Waymo city launches) is a persistent negative drift factor. Net: no directional edge; I center at ~$69.8 (essentially today's price) with lognormal sigma 11% (monthly vol 35%/3.5 = 10%, widened slightly for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$4.93 after 10% haircut x 16x = $79) and EV/EBITDA (NTM adj. EBITDA ~$14.7B after 7% haircut x 11x, ~zero net debt ex-Delivery Hero, 2.0B shares = $81). Delivery Hero assumed value-neutral at the price paid.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus may not fully reflect interest on ~EUR14B bridge for Delivery Hero [2,3], the $10B AV program shifting Uber toward fleet ownership [11], and GAAP EPS inflated by equity-revaluation gains ($1.6B in Q2) [1]

Peer median fwd P/E 18.2x (range 8.0-40.3x) [7]; Uber trades 16.8x today [7], Dolphin cites ~15-16x 2027 GAAP NI [21], AVMS 18x [11]. Set below peer median: higher EPS growth (~31% 3Y fcst vs peer ~22%) is offset by unresolved AV disintermediation risk, so no premium is justified

inputs_detail.derivation: AV fleet/depot opex and mobility take-rate pressure (Q1 mobility take rate fell ~4pts on fuel subsidies [21]); adj. EBITDA margin trend 4.9% of GB [1]
Peer median est. fwd EV/EBITDA ~17x, range 9-46x ex-outliers [7]; Uber adj. EBITDA excludes SBC so placed near BKNG/EXPE/CART (10-14x), below median. Today Uber is ~12.9x 2026E / 10.6x 2027E EBITDA
Q2-26 debt $12.7B less cash $5.4B = $7.3B [1]; MarketScreener projects net cash $4.3B end-2027 [5] but buybacks absorb much of FCF; DH debt offset by DH value at price paid [2]
2.05B diluted Q2-26, trending down with buybacks

bear.story: Robotaxi disintermediation becomes the consensus: Waymo hits 1M weekly rides and leans on its own app, Tesla Cybercab scales in TX/FL, Uber's take rate and AV economics disappoint; Delivery Hero leverage plus AV capex weigh. Multiple compresses to ~11x on ~$4.5 EPS.

base.story: Bookings keep growing high-teens, EBITDA +20-25%, FCF >$12B funds buybacks; AV remains <1% of trips and is visibly additive through Uber's network (higher utilization), but the overhang caps the multiple near 15-16x NTM EPS.

bull.story: Aggregator thesis proves out: AV partners (15+) launch through Uber, financing of vehicles moves off balance sheet, DH integration adds scale, and the multiple re-rates toward peer median ~19-20x on ~$5.3 EPS, toward the ~$100 Street mean target.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16x NTM P/E is ~12% below the 18.2x peer median and inside the range; 11x EV/EBITDA is in the bottom third of the peer range (comparable to BKNG/EXPE/CART).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is taken despite Uber's above-median growth (3Y EPS fcst ~31% vs peer median ~22%) and >$10B TTM FCF, because the AV disintermediation risk that is specific to Uber and Lyft remains unresolved through the horizon (Waymo targeting 1M weekly rides, Uber-Waymo contract ending May 2028, the AV program pushing Uber toward owning assets). A modest discount to the median is used; the EBITDA multiple is lower still because Uber's adjusted EBITDA excludes SBC and the AV/fleet costs ahead.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$53 (about 11x my haircut NTM EPS and ~19% under the 52-week low of $65.41) the market would be pricing a structural impairment, not volatility: e.g. Waymo/Tesla pulling supply off the Uber network, mobility take-rate erosion, bookings growth falling below ~12%, or a Delivery Hero financing/leverage problem. That would invalidate the 'AV is additive to the aggregator' base case.

key_uncertainties: Whether AV operators (Waymo, Tesla) route supply through Uber or build their own demand; Waymo's SF share data is ambiguous (Yipit 15% in June 2026 but ODD expansion distorts it)
How much of the $10B AV program ends up on Uber's balance sheet vs financed by third parties

Sector-wide derating of consumer marketplaces (BKNG, LYFT also down ~27-29% y/y) may persist regardless of Uber fundamentals
reasoning: Fundamentals are strong and accelerating: Q2-26 GB $58.0B (+22% cc), adj. EBITDA $2.8B (+33%), TTM FCF >$10B, Q3 guide GB +18-22% and EPS +28-35% [1]. The stock is down ~30% y/y to 16.8x fwd P/E [7] almost entirely on the robotaxi narrative and the asset-heavy turn ($10B AV program, Delivery Hero for $14.8B [2,3,11]). My lane's alternative data mostly says the near-term threat is still small: Waymo runs ~500k paid rides/week on ~4,000 cars [13,8] against roughly 300M Uber trips/week (3.9B per quarter [1]), i.e. ~0.2%; Tesla has ~476 registered robotaxis in Texas, with an unclear driverless share [13], and Manifold gave Tesla only 13% odds of out-fleeting Waymo by Jan 2027 [18]. Waymo fares ran 13% above Uber in Jan 2026 and rose faster into April [14], so robotaxis are not undercutting on price yet. Uber's app downloads jumped in September [15] (single source, treated as weak), and Uber is hiring AV fleet and depot staff [20], which confirms the move toward operating fleets. Against that, Yipit data shows Waymo reaching ~20-27% of in-zone SF trips within ~20 months [17,22,23], and Campbell argues the later decline to 15% is an artefact of the larger service area [16]. That is the bear case: where AVs operate at scale they take share fast, and Waymo may prefer its own app [11,22]. Valuation: P/E $79 and EV/EBITDA $81, blended to $80, inside the peer ranges with no premium. Scenarios $50/$77/$103 at 25/50/25%. I built the ladder from a three-component lognormal mixture (centers 50/77/103, sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.20), which gives a median of ~$76.5 and P(>=70) of ~0.61. That is a modest upward tilt from $69.62, below my fair value, because negative momentum and a sector-wide derating argue for shrinking toward the current price. The overall spread is about 35-40%, in line with realized vol. Research limits: Twelve Data fundamentals were plan-gated, X was searched only indirectly, and forward EV/EBITDA for peers is estimated from trailing figures.
